data.name: Thargelia
data.detailed_description:
Separated by disaster. Connected by decisions. On an unknown planet, how far would you go to survive?

Thargelia is a two-player narrative adventure multiplayer that plunges you into an intense journey of survival, moral choices, and mistrust. When the transport ship Quiron crashes on a hostile and mysterious planet, the crew is split into two groups — strangers to each other, now bound by a shared fate.

You and another player take on the role of unlikely leaders: Apollo and Artemisa. Each awakens in a different section of the wrecked ship, responsible for a group of survivors, limited resources, and urgent decisions. But what you may not realize... is that your choices directly affect the other player's game — and their fate — in real time.

You can choose dialogue and cooperation to escape together, or manipulate, sabotage, and fight to ensure your own survival — even if it comes at the cost of the other group.

A narrative asymmetric multiplayer like no other

In Thargelia, you're not just playing with someone — you're playing through them. The progression is asymmetric: as one player advances more quickly or makes bolder choices, the other’s world changes. Time moves differently, and the consequences can be immediate... or surface when it's already too late.

Branching narratives with multiple endings

The game features several major endings, all shaped by the decisions you make throughout the story. There are no easy answers — only ethical dilemmas, calculated risks, fragile trust, and unexpected betrayals.

Challenges and puzzles that go beyond logic

Along the way, you'll face obstacles that demand reasoning, strategy, and cooperation. Not every puzzle can be solved alone.

Replayability with deeper layers of discovery

Each new playthrough reveals hidden narrative paths, alternate dialogues, unexpected character connections, and endings that challenge your own sense of right and wrong. You won’t play just to survive — but to uncover what really happened aboard Quiron.

Will you be the hero — or someone else's downfall?

In the end, Thargelia is more than a survival story. It’s a narrative mirror of your decisions — and your humanity.

Will you sacrifice a stranger to save your own?
Or will you rise above instinct and build a bridge between two broken worlds?

One thing is certain: someone will remember what you did.



----

Este projeto foi contemplado pelo Edital nº 5/2023 - Produção Audiovisual - Videoclipe, Videodança, Games da Lei Federal Paulo Gustavo.
